**STEP 1 - Scene:** A single whole apple (red-green, with the stem end facing up) sits on a white paper plate. It is photographed from directly above, so the apple shows as a near-circle.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The paper plate is about 20-22 cm across, so I'll use 20 cm. Area = 3.14 × (10)² ≈ 314 cm². The apple's width is about 0.48 of the plate's width, so its top-down footprint is roughly 23% of the plate area.

**STEP 3 - Items:** One whole apple. No oil, dressing, or sauce is visible. The faint pink and yellow marks on the plate are residue, not food.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Apple ≈ 23% of the plate (about 72 cm²). This is the only food on the plate, so the covered share is 23%.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The apple is roughly spherical with a diameter of about 7.5-8 cm. Its volume is about 250-270 ml, which I take as 260 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole fruit is denser than cut pieces, so I use a bulk density of about 0.75 g/ml. 260 ml × 0.75 ≈ 195 g. Rounded to 190 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Raw apple is about 52 kcal per 100 g. 190 g × 0.52 ≈ 99 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A single medium apple weighs about 150-200 g and has roughly 80-100 kcal, so 190 g and about 99 kcal is plausible for this visible item.

Total: about 190 g and about 99 kcal.
